The criteria for making the debate stage will be similar to 2020, when there was also a big field and a dozen debates, the DNC said, and will include meeting polling and other criteria such as grasroots fundraising.

More details are set to be announced in January, including specific times and locations for the debates, the DNC said, though the party determined five debates will be in 2027 and seven in 2028. The final primary debate is planned for March 2028.

For the first time, candidates must pledge to disavow dark money as a condition of making the debate stage, something Martin has pushed for. Corruption in government was a top concern for voters in the midterm elections.

The debate schedule is one of the most closely watched decisions the DNC makes, along with selecting the city for the 2028 convention. Earlier this year, the DNC narrowed the list of cities to Boston, Denver and Philadelphia.

articles.title: The rise and fall and rise again of Jensen Huang
articles.description: Days after resigning while mired in scandal of extra-marital affairs, Nvidia's Jensen Huang is making a remarkable return.
articles.content:
The rise and fall and rise again of Jensen Huang

ByMichael Race, Peter Hoskins and Lucy Hooker, Business reporters
  • Published
    12 November 2026
Updated 7 hours ago

It's being called a comeback for the ages.

For a long time it seemed that Jensen Huang, the leather jacket-clad founder of Nvidia, dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech", could do no wrong.

Then came allegations of two affairs - one with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy - that rocked the world of tech and the global stock market. Huang resigned.

Now, just 11 days later, he's been reinstated by the board, who says it believes he is the right person to lead the company.

So what do we know about the man who is once again at the head of Nvidia, a linchpin in the US's race for technology leadership with China?

Huang may not be a household name on the same level as Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg.

But his role in the tech industry, especially in relation to the explosion of artificial intelligence in the last three years, may prove more consequential. Nvidia dominates the market for the microchips that are used to power the new technology.

The company is at the centre of the AI race between the US and China, the world's tech and economic powerhouses.

Huang enjoyed access to the seats of political power on an unrivalled scale, being courted by both US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping.

His remarkable rise to the top of his profession saw him amass an estimated fortune of close to $200bn earlier this year, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, though that has since dropped to around $105bn.

Despite always donning his trademark all-black outfits and taking a playful approach to investor presentations, Huang has worked for years to present himself as a family man, someone who exemplified the American Dream.

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang and his family moved to the west coast of the US when he was nine years old. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a Master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.

It was at college where he met his wife, Lori Mills. The pair were lab partners and married in 1985, eight years before Huang founded Nvidia.

They have two children, Madison and Spencer, who now both work in senior roles at Nvidia.

The company became a key provider of the computer chips and circuits used for gaming before it expanded in a new direction. It now creates the key processing chips used to power the growing AI technology.

  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after tech giant rocked by second affair allegation

  • Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive?

    • Published
      12 November

Huang has hailed AI as a "new industrial revolution" that is on a par with the advent of electricity. Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company and its customers include the biggest firms on the planet, Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, SpaceX, Tesla, OpenAI and Anthropic, all spending big on its products.

So it is no surprise that at a recent AI summit at the White House, Huang was picked out from a group of 42 to flank the president, alongside Elon Musk, both men with whom Trump has famously close relationships.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on Jensen Huang, told the BBC, referring to the late boss of Apple. He added that Huang was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.

He described him as a "demanding" boss, who "really pushes his people to the limit".

But while Huang is "very brilliant" and a "world-class computer scientist", there's also "a level of arrogance" and "a level of self-deception as well", he said.

Huang had gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, he added, something that was "very important to him".

First reports emerged on 29 October in the New York Times that Huang had conducted a relationship with Alice Huang, no relation. US officials allege the businesswoman associated with Singapore-based firm Megaspeed is a Chinese intelligence asset.

Huang admitted to having been unfaithful to his wife and apologised for hurting their family.

But the reporting of a second affair, with Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare who has worked at Nvidia for 18 years, prompted a board meeting, followed by an announcement that Huang was stepping down.

He'd barely been gone, however, before a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign was launched, reportedly by current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters.

The man himself said he would be "honoured" to return, should the board ask him.

Although initially showing no interest in reinstating him, the board has now done just that, saying his return was "in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers".

articles.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drones in Libya, Zelensky says
articles.description: The Kremlin warns of an "escalation of tensions in the region", but declines to comment directly on the attacks in Libya.
articles.content:
Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drones in Libya, Zelensky says

ByHafsa Khalil and Joe Inwood, World news correspondent
  • Published
    22 November 2026
Updated 7 hours ago

A Russian warship was sunk by Ukrainian drones at a port in Libya on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.

There was an explosion on the warship at the Benghazi naval base in the early morning, while it was docking for fuel and supplies ahead of its return to Russia, local authorities said.

Zelensky added that Ukraine's attack hit a second Russian vessel, a cargo ship which he claimed was being used to transport weapons.

The local health ministry said it had received injured people from a commercial ship that was targeted off the coast of the port. It is not clear whether this is the same vessel as the one Ukraine has claimed responsibility for.

Following the strikes, the Kremlin warned of an "escalation of tensions in the region", but declined to comment directly on the attacks in Libya.

Libya's two governments - the UN-recognised government in the capital, Tripoli, and a rival administration in the east - have both condemned the attack.

The Tripoli foreign ministry said the country would not accept being drawn into the conflict.

It said foreign forces would not be allowed to use Libyan ports and civilian infrastructure for military purposes.

The eastern government, based in Benghazi, called it a violation of maritime safety and an attack on their sovereignty.

Seven naval drones were deployed to target and sink the corvette Merkury, one of Russia's newest ships, Zelensky said in a statement on Monday. He added that a Ka-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed.

The Ukrainian president said the second ship was the MV ANGARA, a Russian container carrier.

The attack came the day after a Russian cargo vessel was hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland. The Sparta II had been bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning.

Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely to be behind the attack. Kyiv has not commented.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Monday that the "expansion of terrorist activity in the Baltic" was a "dangerous trend" and has said "it is, of course, leading to an escalation of tensions in the region."

When questioned over the attacks in Libya, Peskov said information would be provided by the country's defence ministry and added: "We paid attention to Zelensky's statements about it".

Peskov declined to comment on the strikes on Russian ships in Libya and said that that information would be provided by Russia's Defence Ministry.

The UN mission in Libya expressed "serious concern" over the attacks on Sunday, calling for "an immediate, independent and transparent investigation".

"Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts," the UNSMIL wrote on X., external

Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship that was struck in the morning engulfed in flames and smoke. Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC also shows a boat on fire at 05:47 GMT at the Benghazi port.

US-based intelligence firm Vantor collected high-resolution images that it said showed Project 20380 Steregushchiy-class corvette (Merkury) - a Russian navy ship - moored in the port on Saturday, and on Sunday showed most of the same ship capsized and sunk with only the forward bow still visible.

Neither of Libya's rival administrations has formally declared support for either side in the Russia-Ukraine war, but they have contrasting ties with Moscow and Kyiv.

The head of the Libyan National Army, which controls much of the east of the country, has longstanding links with Russia.

The eastern-based Government of National Stability (GNS) said the Russian ship - which it did not name or identify - was using the Benghazi port within the framework of an existing maritime agreement.

Sunday's incident is under investigation, and authorities are coordinating with their Russian counterparts to determine the source of the suspected attack and who is responsible for it, GNS added.

It said Libya was not party to the Russia-Ukraine war, or any other conflict beyond its borders.

GNS has accused the Tripoli-based Government of National Unity (GNU) of hosting Ukrainian military personnel and allowing them to operate from Libyan territory against Russian targets.

Separately, the GNU warned against hosting foreign forces and allowing them to use facilities in a statement published by state media.

It said such activity raises "serious fears" about "risks that may result from involving ports and civilian facilities in activities related to external conflicts, and the resulting threat to the lives of citizens and the safety of national facilities and assets".

Libya fractured into violence and instability after its leader Muammar Gaddafi was overthrown in 2011, leading to the opposing governments.

Benghazi is more than 2,000 km (1,243 miles) away from the Russian capital Moscow.

In March, Russia accused Ukraine of targeting the Russian tanker Arctic Metagaz in the Mediterranean between Libya and Malta with "uncrewed sea drones" launched from the Libyan coast.

As well as having an economic impact on Russia, hampering the ability of their so-called shadow fleet of tankers to export oil and gas, attacks like this are seen as humiliating to the Kremlin, according to Dr Jalel Harchaoui of the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI).

But it is not only Moscow that will want to react to this latest incident. The ship was in the region as part of a deal with the government of eastern Libya - allied with Khalifa Haftar, commander of the Libyan National Army.

Harchaoui said Haftar will take the attack as a personal slight. "You're going to have a response by the Haftar family. They will ask questions about who is hosting the Ukrainians."

articles.title: The Incredible, Elegant DNA Repair System Makes Gene Editing Work
articles.description: Genetic information is sturdy, but its physical structure is sensitive. Natural tools for repairing a cell’s thousands of daily injuries are fundamental to gene-editing technologies. The post The Incredible, Elegant DNA Repair System Makes Gene Editing Work first appeared on Quanta Magazine
articles.content:
By Annie Melchor

Contributing Writer

November 23, 2026

biology DNA explainers genes genetics genome molecular biology All topics

Humans have debated the meaning of life for many millennia, but from evolution’s perspective, it is simple: Preserve the genome. Of course, mutation is allowed, as is the genetic mixing and matching of sexual reproduction, to create variety and evolutionary diversity. But we all exist because a viable lineage of DNA has persisted for 4 billion years. The genome’s policy is typically, “If the code works, don’t change it.”

You’d think, then, that cells would keep their DNA under lock and key, protected from the elements like the precious blueprint it is. But this isn’t possible. DNA is a working document. Cells need near-constant access to these instructions for making the molecules required by life. The huge, complex molecular structure is therefore exposed to nonstop assault by the by-products of everyday cellular metabolism, as well as environmental factors, such as radiation (including ultraviolet and X-ray), alcohol, pesticides, and more.

“DNA damage occurs all the time,” said Björn Schumacher, a molecular biologist at the University of Cologne. “[DNA] contains all the information for building a cell, building an organism, maintaining cells and tissues, and all that — but yet it is surprisingly unstable.”

He estimates that some cells endure up to 100,000 DNA damage events every day. “Damage to the DNA is the default,” he said. These events can injure sections of the DNA molecule — or, worse, break the strand in half. Even minor DNA damage risks changing or destroying the essential instructions a cell needs to operate, which can make cells malfunction, die, or become cancerous.

However, many of those tens of thousands of daily lesions get repaired quickly. Cells have native repair mechanisms that recognize and replace faulty DNA before lasting damage and dysfunction set in. In fact, the ability to repair damaged or broken DNA had to evolve at essentially the same time as DNA, Schumacher said, “because you cannot have stable genetic information without DNA repair.”

These mechanisms are essential not only to the evolutionary lineage of all known life, but also to promising technologies to treat genetic diseases. Scientists and doctors who experiment with gene editing must rely on DNA’s natural self-editing and repair tools to insert, delete, or mutate genes to study and treat disease.

So perhaps instead of a master blueprint protected behind glass, it’s better to imagine DNA as a beloved cookbook that is constantly in use. While it’s open on the kitchen counter, it’s bound to get splattered with sauce — or even have a page ripped. But spills can be wiped off. Torn pages can be taped up. And a smear obscuring an odd ingredient might even improve a recipe.

Do the Twist

To understand how DNA gets damaged so easily, we need to see its structure, beyond the impossible elegance of the double helix. Most DNA is packed into chromosomes, dense structures formed by long, delicate filaments of DNA wrapped tightly around proteins. If you were to unwrap the DNA and untwist its double helix, you’d see a ladder made of nucleotides: the building blocks of DNA.

A single DNA strand — one side rail and half of each rung — encodes a specific arrangement of the four nucleotides, also known as bases. Each is a complex molecule represented by a single letter: A, T, G, or C. Across from it is a backup on the opposite, complementary strand, made up of each nucleotide’s natural partner (A’s partner is T, and G’s is C). The “rungs” of the DNA ladder are held together with relatively weak, transient bonds that allow the helix to be opened and closed like a zipper, so enzymes can access, read, and copy the code.

LONDON (AP) — More than 12,000 fans were evacuated from a concert by American rapper Don Toliver and over 80 were treated by medics after an unknown irritant was released in the crowd, authorities in the English city of Manchester said Monday.

Greater Manchester Police said officers were called around 10 p.m. (2200 GMT) Sunday to the Co-op Live arena after reports of people being affected by a substance, initially believed to be tear gas. Footage shared on social media appeared to show concertgoers coughing and covering their mouths as they left the venue.

The force declared a "major incident," which allows different emergency services to coordinate their response.

Concertgoer Ben Stevenson told the Manchester Evening News he was in the standing area of the arena when he "started coughing and (my) eyes were kind of itchy."

He said Toliver left the stage and the venue lights came on, but it was not until almost an hour later that an announcement said, "due to an unforeseen issue, the show is over, and please make your way out at your own pace."

Joey Howe, a concertgoer, told BBC Radio Manchester that there was a "horrible smell" and people rushed out of the venue.

"People were coming through in wheelchairs, choking. It was really distressing," he said.

READ MORE: French police fire tear gas as more than 250,000 protest nationwide for school funding

One person was taken to a hospital and more than 80 were assessed at the scene, with some reporting eye and respiratory symptoms, the North West Ambulance Service said.

It said "decontamination is being carried out as a precaution" at the venue.

Police Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker said: "Anyone who has left the event and since become unwell is advised to attend their local hospital."

"We will now begin to fully understand what this substance was and how this incident came about," she said.

Co-op Live, which opened in 2024, is about 2 miles (3.2 kilometers) from Manchester Arena, where 22 people were killed when a bomber blew himself up during an Ariana Grande concert in 2017.
Co-op Live said in a statement that venue bosses were working with police to identify the cause of the incident.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham's spokesman, Tom Wells, said the incident was "deeply worrying" and "many families will understandably be anxious this morning." He urged people to let police conduct a full investigation.

Grammy Award- nominated trap and R&B rapper-singer Toliver, who features on the soundtrack to the new "Grand Theft Auto" game, is scheduled to perform at London's O2 Arena on Monday and Wembley Arena on Tuesday as part of his Nitrous tour.

articles.title: Prominent Zimbabwean preacher arrested on sexual assault allegations
articles.description: Uebert Angel, a British-Zimbabwean national, leads a charismatic church with branches in several countries.
articles.content:
Prominent Zimbabwean preacher arrested on sexual assault allegations

ByKhanyisile Ngcobo
Reporting fromJohannesburg
  • Published
    8 hours ago

A well-known Zimbabwean preacher has been arrested on indecent assault and sodomy allegations, local police said.

Uebert Angel, who leads an international charismatic church with branches around the world, was arrested during a church service in Harare on Sunday. Pictures and footage of the dramatic arrest have since been circulated online.

In one video, a convoy of vehicles is seen escorting the self-styled prophet as he sits in the back of a police van surrounded by armed police officers.

The controversial founder of Spirit Embassy was also appointed Zimbabwe's special presidential envoy and ambassador-at-large to Europe and the Americas back in 2021 by President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

In 2023, he made headlines when an undercover report by Al Jazeera claimed that he had offered to use his diplomatic status to launder large amounts of money through a gold-smuggling scheme in the country.

According to the Qatar-based network, Angel, 48, told reporters working undercover that the scheme was approved by President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Zimbabwean police only released a brief statement confirming his arrest but a member of his team told reporters the British Zimbabwean national was still in police custody and it was unclear when he'd make an appearance in court.

"It can be in the afternoon or tomorrow [Tuesday]. We are still within the legal framework [for him to appear in court]," Professor Lovemore Madhuku told state-owned broadcaster ZBC in a clip posted online.

This is not the first time the prominent preacher has been accused of improper behaviour.

A report by local online publication ZimLIVE in 2021 said that Angel had previously faced allegations of sexual impropriety from several women, at least five of whom are in England. The charismatic preacher has denied the allegations, the outlet added at the time.

Angel's church has branches in Zimbabwe, South Africa and the UK and he known for his ties to other African preachers like Malawian televangelist Shepherd Bushiri.

articles.title: Mexican soldiers attacked in wake of drug lord's arrest
articles.description: Eight suspects are arrested after firing on soldiers trying to re-establish order following the arrest of 'El Chapo Isidro'.
articles.content:
Mexican soldiers attacked in wake of drug lord's arrest

ByVanessa Buschschlüter
Latin America online editor
  • Published
    23 November 2026, 13:26 GMT
Updated 8 hours ago

Mexican soldiers have detained eight alleged members of a drug cartel whose leader was arrested on Friday, sparking a wave of violence in northern Sinaloa state.

The Mexican defence ministry said the soldiers were shot by the suspects on Sunday while on patrol in the town of Sinaloa de Leyva, trying to re-establish order in the wake of the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores.

Meza Flores, also known as "Chapo Isidro", was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list and had managed to evade capture for years.

The ministry said the eight had also been involved in the retaliatory violence unleashed by Meza Flores's cartel in the hours after his arrest on Friday.

In a statement published on social media, external, the ministry of defence said that one of the detainees was under age.

It added that its special forces had seized six vehicles as part of their operation, two of which had been fitted with bullet-proof armour and gun turrets.

The US Department of Justice described Friday's arrest of Meza Flores as "a spectacular military operation" and congratulated Mexico's military and special forces on his capture.

It said that the US Homeland Security Task Force had supported the Mexican military and praised the "bilateral effort".

Mexico's defence ministry said its special forces had used stealth and surprise to reach the home of the wanted man.

They also established a security perimeter to prevent Meza Flores from escaping and cartel reinforcements from arriving.

Nevertheless, a bloody firefight ensued, in which four soldiers and 16 "members of organised crime" were killed, according to the latest figure released by the defence minister on Monday.

Along with Meza Flores, his second-in-command, known as "Serafín", and his financial operator, were also arrested and quickly transferred by air to Mexico City.

As news of their arrest spread, members of their cartel erected barricades on major roads and set cars and some shops alight.

There were also reports of shoot-outs between the security forces and cartel members.

Who is 'Chapo Isidro'?

US Assistant Attorney General A Tysen Duva has described Meza Flores as "the most dangerous man in Mexico".

"For decades Meza Flores has promoted the terrorist objectives of the Sinaloa cartel," Duva said, accusing him of "flooding the United States with deadly substances".

The 44-year-old is believed to have started his criminal career with the Juárez cartel decades ago.

He later moved on to become the right-hand man of the leader of the Beltrán Leyva Organisation, a drug gang once allied to the Sinaloa cartel before the two groups split and became bitter enemies.

As early as 2013, the US Treasury identified Meza Flores as the leader of his own drug-trafficking organisation, named after him.

The US Treasury said at the time, that the Meza Flores drug trafficking organisation was responsible for "the distribution of large quantities of methamphetamine, heroin, marijuana, and cocaine to the United States".

It added that the turf war between the Meza Flores cartel and the Sinaloa cartel had "resulted in the quadrupling of drug-war killings" in between 2009 and 2013.

According to think tank Insight Crime, external, Meza Flores himself kept a low profile over the last decade while continuing to run his cartel out of Guasave, in Sinaloa state.

The head of the US Drug Enforcement Administration said that his capture was a "significant blow to a ruthless criminal organisation that has used extreme violence to traffic deadly drugs, including fentanyl, a designated weapon of mass destruction, into American communities".

His arrest, and the co-operation between US and Mexican officials which led to it, will be seen as a win for the government of Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum.

Sheinbaum has stressed that she is keen to work with the US authorities to capture high-profile target as long as Mexican's sovereignty is respected.

articles.title: Trump claims credit as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
articles.description: President Trump endorsed the announcement, calling it essential for the success of the company and the economy. He added that the government does not see Jensen's return as a national security risk.
articles.content:
Jensen Huang is back atop Nvidia after the chipmaker's board reinstated him as president, chief executive and board director. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said in a statement. Nadja Wohlleben/Getty Images/Getty Images Europe hide caption

Nadja Wohlleben/Getty Images/Getty Images Europe

Sign up for alerts on breaking news and exclusive reporting from NPR.

Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO of the world's largest chipmaker on Monday, sending the company's stock soaring as President Trump claimed credit for brokering his close ally's return.

It was a stunning reversal of fortune for Huang. He resigned less than two weeks ago, following news reports of extramarital affairs, including with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies suspected of being a Chinese spy.

In a statement put out just before the market opened, Nvidia said its board voted unanimously in favor of bringing back Huang after a series of conversations and meetings, as well as input from people at "senior levels" of the U.S. government. "Based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk," the board said.

Sponsor Message

Nvidia's stock price shot up more than 30% on Monday, helping buoy stock indexes after last week's losses, which were driven by the tech sector.

Trump endorsed the board's move, calling it the "correct and proper decision" in a social media post. He said Huang's leadership was needed "in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy."

Business

The AI boom had a really bad week — and it's raising loud alarms

The president had repeatedly urged Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang as CEO in public comments and on social media. In a lengthy interview with CNBC Monday morning, Trump claimed his influence helped Huang get his job back.

"I don't want to say, but basically I was represented at the board," the president said, in response to a question about a report in Semafor that he had called directly into the NVIDIA board meeting.

"I spoke to them. Let me just put it that way. And I convinced them," Trump told CNBC. "And I must tell you, it was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago."

He later added: "When the stock starts dropping forty, fifty percent, it was a lot easier for me to do it yesterday than it would have been."

Sponsor Message

Huang stepped down amid a growing scandal

Nvidia, which Huang co-founded and has run for the past 33 years, dominates the market for the chips used to train and run artificial intelligence. Trump and Huang have grown close during the president's second term in office, with Huang becoming one of the most influential business leaders with the president's ear on AI policy. He has successfully lobbied the U.S. government to allow chipmakers to sell some chips to China, although Nvidia's most advanced chips are subject to export controls.

Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov. 12 after news reports that he had affairs with multiple women, including an Nvidia executive who reported to him. But the most explosive allegation was that he'd engaged in a relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that was buying Nvidia chips, whom U.S. officials believed had ties to Chinese intelligence.

The Justice Department has said it is conducting a criminal investigation of Megaspeed for potential chip smuggling. In a statement sent to NPR on Nov. 15, Megaspeed said it "conducts legitimate and lawful business," and that Alice Huang left the company in 2025, but that it is conducting an internal investigation.

Nvidia's board said as recently as Nov. 17 that it did not intend to reinstate Huang, though Huang publicly said he would return if the board allowed it. On Monday, board chair Harvey Jones said in a statement: "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers."

The board said on Monday its turnaround followed a series of meetings with Huang that left them satisfied with his "candor and ability to lead" the company. It said its investigation into Huang and the allegations he had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort continues and that Huang is "committed to cooperating with it."

Sponsor Message

"I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement on Monday. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment."

Trump dismisses national security concerns

On Monday, Trump said that the government has "no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," and that Attorney General Todd Blanche says the U.S. "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."

Last week Nvidia's board said it had formed a committee to oversee the company's national security policies, compliance with U.S. export controls, and risk management of global trade.

Huang is expected to testify before congressional committees next week.

To explain why it was so important that Huang remain at Nvidia's helm, Trump told CNBC he feared China attempting to bring his expertise to their country.

"I could see China coming in and saying to Jensen, 'Hey, how would you like to come to China?' He's got a little blood in him, you know. He's got a little blood there. 'How would you like to come to China and head up Huawei, okay, and head up one of our companies?'" Trump said. "And you know what? If Jensen was angry enough, if he was treated badly, maybe he could do that."

When CNBC asked Trump if he wasn't worried after he was alerted that Huang was in a relationship with a potential spy, Trump demurred, saying, "I won't get into it."

Following the CNBC interview, Trump celebrated Huang's reinstatement on Truth Social by posting a doctored image invoking a famous photo of the president after the assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania, in 2024. In the posted image, Huang is in President Trump's place with blood spattered on his face, raising his fist — holding a red bra — as an Nvidia flag waves in the background.

articles.title: Nigeria's president says he is also hit by water and power cuts plaguing country
articles.description: Bola Tinubu says he was shaving last week when the water cut out - an experience familiar to many Nigerians.
articles.content:
Nigeria's president says he is also hit by water and power cuts plaguing country

ByMansur Abubakar
Reporting fromAbuja
  • Published
    23 November 2026, 11:15 GMT
Updated 9 hours ago

Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu says the presidential villa suffers from cuts in electricity and water - issues that are all too common for the country's ordinary citizens.

He said he was shaving last week when the water supply cut at the villa, known as Aso Rock, in Abuja.

He is seeking re-election next January and vowed to address these issues.

Tinubu made the disclosure on Sunday at a special prayer session organised in his honour by members of his family in Lagos.

He explained: "On the Wednesday of last week, I was shaving, and the water went off. In the villa, you won't know punishment dey dia too [there’s punishment there too in Nigerian pidgin].

"The water went off. So we will correct all this. No light, no water, no electricity, no development. We have just started. We can do it, and we will do it for Nigeria,” he said.

Aso Villa serves as both the office and official residence of the Nigerian president. It is situated at the base of Aso Rock in Abuja.

Last year, 10bn naira (£5.5m; $7.2m), was allocated in the budget for the installation of a solar mini-grid in the Aso Villa as part of efforts to address rising electricity bills and unstable power supply.

Some reports say it has been completed and is in the testing phase, with plans to fully disconnect the facility from the national grid soon.

  • Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

    • Published
      12 November

  • Search and rescue teams race against time after Nigeria boat tragedy

    • Published
      10 hours ago

Nigeria has long endured electricity shortages, but recent severe disruptions have been caused primarily by insufficient gas supplies and declining hydropower output, rather than the usual nationwide grid collapse.

Persistent blackouts in Lagos, Abuja and elsewhere have forced distribution companies to implement rotating power cuts, severely impacting households and businesses.

The country also suffers from chronic water shortages, the result of a structural crisis rooted in the gap between rapid urban population growth and decaying, inadequate public water infrastructure, leaving millions without reliable supplies, especially in Lagos.

Tinubu made a high-profile electricity promise during the 2023 election campaign, but the exact wording and how binding it is has become a major point of contention ahead of the election on 16 January 2027.

In 2022, months before the last presidential election, Tinubu said: "Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills any more. A promise made will be a promise kept.

"If I don't keep the promise and I come for a second term, don't vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn't deliver,” he said.

Despite the continuing power cuts, some of his supporters point to improved electricity supplies in rural areas as well as a recently approved $2bn (£1.5bn) investment in a new East–West Super Grid, designed to expand electricity transmission capacity and strengthen the national grid, as evidence that he is doing his best to keep to his promise.

Tinubu defeated the country’s former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as well as former Anambra state governor Peter Obi in 2023 and the three are seen as the strongest contenders once again.

articles.title: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya
articles.description: Ukrainian forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
articles.content:
By —

Hanna Arhirova, Associated Press Hanna Arhirova, Associated Press

By —

Samy Magdy, Associated Press Samy Magdy, Associated Press

  • https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/zelenskyy-hails-ukraines-attack-on-a-russian-warship-docked-at-a-naval-base-in-libya

Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya

World Nov 23, 2026 9:13 AM EST

KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that maritime drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day.

Ukrainian forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Zelenskyy. The ship, the Merkury, was one of Russia's newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbor, he said in a post on X.

READ MORE: Poland says Russia allegedly twice tried to kill a Ukrainian American rapper

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to comment on the attack, saying that Russia's Defense Ministry would provide more information "if deemed to be appropriate."

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometers (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces.

Ukraine has at times embarrassed Moscow during the war with attacks such as Operation Spiderweb in June 2025, when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft parked at air bases across Russia. Along the roughly 1,250-kilometer (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine, Kyiv's drones and ground robots are helping hold back Russia's bigger army.

At the same time, Russia's missiles and drones have devastated Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter and damaged civilian buildings.

READ MORE: NATO calls Russian missiles landing in Poland a 'grave violation' of airspace

A Russian strike on a five-story apartment block in a village near Kyiv killed 11 people, regional police said Monday. A 7-year-old child and a 79-year-old woman were pulled alive from the rubble after the Sunday morning attack, rescue services said.

Three people were killed Monday in a Russian strike on a hospital in the city of Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine, the regional military administration said. Two other people were killed when Russian forces struck a vehicle that bore markings indicating it was evacuating residents from the eastern city of Kramatorsk, authorities said.

Zelenskyy lauds Ukrainian attacks from Siberia to Libya

Zelenskyy described Sunday's attack as "exemplary" and said "the targets we set were achieved."

"We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons," he said.

Ukraine has hit Russian oil refineries as far away as western Siberia and Russian warships in the Mediterranean, Zelenskyy noted in a video address to a meeting of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

An oil refinery in Russia's western Rostov region halted work Monday after what Gov. Yuri Slyusar said was a "massive" Ukrainian drone and missile attack that lasted more than six hours. Ukraine's General Staff said the refinery, located just a few dozen kilometers (miles) from the Ukrainian border, can process up to 55 million barrels of oil a year and was on fire after the attack.

"We keep finding ways to get back on our feet after every Russian attack," Zelenskyy said.

Ukrainian forces also struck the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Zelenskyy said Moscow used to transport weapons. He added that the forces also destroyed a Ka-27 military helicopter that was on the Merkury.

Ukrainian forces are operating in western Libya under a covert deal endorsed by the West, using the North African country's territory to strike a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean in March, according to Libyan officials.

The Ukrainian forces, most of them drone experts, were operating mainly at an air base in the coastal city of Misrata, but also in other military facilities in the capital of Tripoli and the coastal town of Zawiya, the officials told The Associated Press earlier this year. They spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential matters.

READ MORE: 'The symbol of the occupation': Ukraine destroys span of Kerch Bridge linking Russia with Crimea

Sunday's attack severely damaged the Russian corvette at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya, according to two Libyan officials, although Zelenskyy claimed it was sunk.

Benghazi residents heard loud explosions and saw flames at the base early Sunday. Civil defense units rushed to the site and extinguished the fire, authorities in eastern Libya said.

The vessel had docked to refuel and take on supplies as part of an agreement between Russia and the eastern-based government in Libya, a statement said without providing details about the vessel or its cargo.

The government in eastern Libya sent a letter to U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres and the U.N. Security Council, calling for an international investigation into the potential use of western Libya to prepare and launch the attack.

Libyan officials say 2 sea drones hit Russian warship

Libyan officials who were briefed on the attack told AP that at least four drones were intercepted while two hit the corvette, which is designed to patrol coastal waters and escort other ships.

At least 10 people, including Libyan and Russian nationals, were wounded in the attack, one of the officials said.

The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.

READ MORE: Kushner says Russia is 'comfortable' with NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine to end war after Trump talks with Putin

Ambrey, a U.K.-based maritime security and risk intelligence firm, said that some of the explosions at the Benghazi Naval Base were likely caused by the detonation of ammunition aboard the Merkury.

Hours after the warship attack, another sea drone strike hit a Maltese-flagged commercial vessel sailing off Benghazi, the Libyan coast guard said.

The Russian cargo ship was sanctioned, Ukraine says

Ukraine's Security Service, or SBU, said the cargo ship MV Angara was sanctioned and used to transport Russian military equipment, while the Merkury regularly escorted Russian naval convoys, including guarding the MV Angara.

The drones were delivered to a designated location and launched from a "mother ship" near the target, the SBU said.

Russian defenses tried to intercept the attacking drones, it said.

"Ukraine's defense forces have once again shown that the Russian navy and its logistics have no safe routes," the SBU said.

Magdy reported from Cairo. Associated Press writers Katie Marie Davies in Manchester, England, and Barry Hatton in Lisbon, Portugal, contributed.

articles.title: Nvidia board unanimously reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman
articles.description: Trump, who has a close personal relationship with Huang, called for the reinstatement as recently as Sunday night and took credit for the board's decision in an interview Monday with CNBC.
articles.content:
By —

Kaitlyn Huamani, Associated Press Kaitlyn Huamani, Associated Press

By —

Aamer Madhani, Associated Press Aamer Madhani, Associated Press

  • https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/nvidia-board-unanimously-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-ceo-and-chairman
  • Email
  • Facebook

Share on Facebook Share on Twitter

Nvidia board unanimously reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman

Nation Updated on Nov 23, 2026 2:50 PM EST — Published on Nov 23, 2026 9:10 AM EST

In a surprise move, Nvidia's board on Monday reinstated CEO Jensen Huang, apparently at the behest of President Donald Trump, just days after rejecting Huang's offer to return to the chipmaker where he was a leading evangelist for artificial intelligence.

The sudden reversal was the latest twist in the fallout from Huang's admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," board Chairman Harvey C. Jones said in a statement.

Trump, who has a close personal relationship with Huang, called for the reinstatement as recently as Sunday night and took credit for the board's decision in an interview Monday with CNBC.

READ MORE: What Trump told PBS News about Jensen Huang before Nvidia reinstatement

"I believe my intervention was very important," Trump said.

The president said he spoke to Huang about the reinstatement Sunday, and the CEO assured him that he would work harder than before his fall. Trump also said his administration assured Nvidia that there were no national security concerns about Huang's return.

"The board decided to do what we wanted them to do," the president said.

Trump declined to say whether he called into the board meeting, though he said, "Basically, I was represented at the board."

Vice President JD Vance stepped up his involvement over the weekend in making Trump's case to the Nvidia board, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

The person, who was not authorized to comment publicly and spoke on the condition of anonymity, said the White House believed that Vance, who worked in Silicon Valley before jumping into politics, had the stature to serve as an effective emissary in helping Nvidia board members overcome reservations about rehiring Huang.

Nvidia plays a crucial role in the AI industry, dominating the market for computer chips used to train and run AI models. It also has many partnerships and investments in companies that purchase its chips.

Huang still faces scrutiny

The reinstatement does not clear Huang of further scrutiny, including several congressional investigations, over the affair and the suspected diversion of Nvidia's advanced chips to China. Huang is scheduled to sit for an interview next week with three House committees investigating the scandal's implications for national security.

Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer said the administration's rush to reinstate Huang "underscores the need for Congress to act."

"Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing" by the administration, Huang, other Nvidia executives and "anyone selling out our national security for financial gain," Schumer said in a statement.

WATCH: Trump says he would love former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to 'be given a second chance'

Huang, who will also serve as Nvidia president, said in a statement that he was "honored" to return to the company and that he resumes the responsibility "with the greatest humility and renewed commitment." He thanked Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress, who will return to her role as chief financial officer, as well as Nvidia's executive staff for their leadership during the brief period of disorder.

"I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support," Huang's statement said. "Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work."

Huang returned Monday to Nvidia headquarters in Silicon Valley, and employees gathered in the building's atrium loudly cheered him on, as shown on an employee video broadcast on CNBC.

"I am going to be a better CEO the second time around," Huang said.

Nvidia leads a rally on Wall Street

Shares of Nvidia soared 33% to $165.57 at the opening bell Monday, moments after Huang's return was announced. That price was far below the all-time high of $239.24 that the stock reached just last month.

That helped end a seven-day losing streak that had dragged the S&P 500 into correction territory. Wall Street delivered a tremendous rally, with the S&P surging 4.8%, the Nasdaq climbing 6.6% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising 3.2% in early afternoon trading.

Trump, in the CNBC interview, acknowledged that the stock market's declines last week — one of the worst weeks since the 2008 financial crisis — "probably" impacted his thinking on Huang.

The president said Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed that the government "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."

Trump called the reinstatement the "correct and proper decision," writing on social media Monday that the country "needs Jensen's leadership" at the company "in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy." He also called for Nvidia to continue its internal investigation.

Trump also posted a fake photo of Huang, modeled off images of the president defiantly raising his fist after surviving an assassination attempt, with the tech mogul grasping a red bra in his clenched hand.

Announcement follows a whirlwind month for Nvidia

The company has had a whirlwind month after Huang admitted to at least one extramarital affair, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, a suspected spy for the country. Nvidia stock was at the center of market volatility in the wake of the admission and its downstream effects in Washington.

Blanche told reporters at an unrelated news conference this month that the Justice Department had not reached any conclusion about whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy.

"All that I think I will say is that of course DOJ is investigating or looking at it," Blanche said.

The Justice Department is conducting a criminal investigation involving potential export control violations at Megaspeed, the Singapore-based cloud computing firm where Alice Huang was an executive.

Jensen Huang's reinstatement came after days of speculation about whether he would return.

Supporters set up an online petition calling for him to get his job back that drew many signatures from current and former Nvidia staff, investors and other Silicon Valley supporters, including Elon Musk.

Huang posted an online message last week saying he would be "honored" to return if the company asked him. But the board responded then that it did not intend to reinstate him.

It's not the first time a tech industry leader has been fired because of transparency concerns and then quickly rehired after an outpouring of support from staff and investors. Three years ago, OpenAI co-founder Sam Altman was ousted as CEO after a chaotic power struggle and then reinstated days later after employees revolted.

Associated Press writers Kelvin Chan and Eric Tucker contributed.

articles.title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'
articles.description: 21-year-old Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty to the Rockstar Games hack and others he carried out when he was a teenager.
articles.content:
GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

ByJoe Tidy
Cyber correspondent, World Service, Reporting fromWoolwich Crown Court
  • Published
    23 November 2026, 14:08 GMT
Updated 9 hours ago

A cyber criminal who hacked the maker of Grand Theft Auto has been released on licence on the same day as being sentenced to 7 years in prison.

Multiple offender Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford, was released from custody with the judge warning him: "Don't let this happen again."

The now 21-year-old hacked several companies and individuals, including GTA 6-maker Rockstar Games, whom he tried to extort after stealing clips of the unfinished game in 2022.

Kurtaj had pleaded guilty last Monday at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.

Kurtaj was originally sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital due to the severity of his autism.

But, in an unusual move, he was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial and released to a normal prison in January.

Now, he has been sentenced and released on the same day as the judge considered his hospital stay and remand in prison long enough.

He has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order which will last five years. It restricts his activity online including barring him from using Telegram and Discord.

City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online".

He hacked Rockstar games, Revolut and Uber while on bail and under police protection in a Travelodge in Bicester.

He was there for protection from rival hackers who had threatened to attack him for his stolen stashes of Bitcoin.

With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj hacked Rockstar using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished GTA 6, which had been shrouded in secrecy until its release last week.

He then broke into the company's internal Slack messaging system to declare: "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code."

The company refused to co-operate so he posted the clips and source code on a forum under the username TeaPotUberHacker.

Rockstar Games said it cost the firm $5m (£3.8m) to recover from the hack, plus thousands of hours of staff time.

The company also said the breach revealed for the first time that one of the playable characters in the game was a woman - a secret it was guarding closely for marketing purposes.

When he was sentenced he stood and smiled.

He had short hair and an unkempt beard and wore a suit and buttoned-up white shirt without a tie.

The hacker blinked frequently during the hearing.

The Judge Mr Justice Turner told him "you are a very talented young man," and warned him: "Don't let this happen again."

Kurtaj's defence team said he found the online world a more comfortable way of interacting with other people.

"The restricted and repetitive patterns of behaviour and interests that are a core feature of ASD [autism spectrum disorder] led him to become preoccupied with the online world where he felt better able to function and exist," they said.

They said he was exposed to people who showed him how to cheat at games and then to "people who were involved in hacking".

During the pandemic, he was "very isolated" and his "connection to Lapsus$ provided him with a sense of community and self-worth that had been absent in his life previously," they added.

Kurtaj and the gang's other hacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber used social engineering techniques - tricking people into clicking malicious links or giving up sensitive information - to gain access to internal systems.

Previously, the court heard that during his hack on Uber he posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.

His hacks on the companies are estimated to have caused around £10m of damage.

Using the data stolen from the firms, he and other members of the gang targeted cryptocurrency investors.

The prosecution argued that the gang stole at least $300,000 (£230,000) from individual victims.

Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to physical assaults on workers while in custody, including multiple biting incidents.

In prison, he was caught with a mobile phone after sending a taunting text message to police and posting updates on Snapchat.

articles.title: Welfare cuts: What's been happening with Pip and universal credit?
articles.description: The government commissioned a review into Pip last year after it was forced to water down planned cuts to benefits.
articles.content:
Welfare cuts: What's been happening with Pip and universal credit?

  • Published
    17 March 2025
Updated 9 hours ago

The assessment process of a key disability benefit should be overhauled to "better recognise people's varying costs and needs", the disability minister has said.

Sir Stephen Timms has been leading a review into Personal Independence Payments (Pip) and has called the current system "not fit for purpose".

The review was commissioned by the government last year after it was forced to water down planned cuts to benefits in the face of fierce opposition from backbench Labour MPs.

What is Pip and what is it worth?

Pip is paid to 3.7 million people with a long-term physical or mental health condition, external in England and Wales.

It is not linked to someone's savings or income and does not affect other benefits, or the benefit cap, external. People can get Pip if they are working.

Pip includes a daily living component and a mobility component. Claimants may be eligible for one or both.

The daily living payments are:

  • a standard rate of £76.70 per week

  • an enhanced rate of £114.60 per week

The mobility payments - which are not affected by the changes - are:

  • a standard rate of £30.30 per week

  • an enhanced rate of £80.00 per week

What is happening to Pip?

In March 2025, the government, under former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer, announced plans to tighten daily living assessments for both current and future Pip claimants.

However, after more than 120 Labour MPs threatened to vote against the legislation, the government said those already receiving Pip would not be affected.

The original proposals said that people with the highest levels of a permanent condition or disability would no longer have to be reassessed at all.

The assessments involve questions about everyday tasks, with each scored from zero, for no difficulty, to 12, for most difficulty.

For example, needing help to wash your hair, or your body below the waist scores two points, but needing help to wash between the shoulders and waist is worth four points.

The government said originally that anyone claiming Pip for the first time after November 2026 would have to score at least four points for a single activity, rather than across a range of different ones.

However, this change was delayed until the wider Timms review of Pip. The final report - which will include recommendations - is due to be published on Tuesday.

The cost of Pip is forecast to rise to more than £41bn by 2030. The cuts originally proposed by the government aimed to save about £5.5bn a year by the end of the decade.

However, the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) and Resolution Foundation said the concessions made by the government meant it would make no "net savings" by 2029-30.

Sir Timms's review is expected to recommend people with the most severe conditions have a "fast track" process which is "less burdensome".

His long-awaited review comes after another review by former Labour Health Secretary Alan Milburn, who proposed reforms that involved changing benefits to tackle the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (Neet).

The government welcomed the Milburn review, which included a recommendation to move those aged 18 to 24 off Pip and the health element of universal credit, and onto an entirely new benefits system.

  • Humiliation for Starmer as he loses control of Commons

    • Published
      2 July 2025

  • What has been driving the rise in disability benefit claims?

    • Published
      30 June 2025

  • 'I don't want to live on benefits, I want to work'

    • Published
      26 June 2025

Any changes to Pip would apply in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

In Scotland, Pip has been replaced with Adult Disability Payment, external.

However, although new Pip rules would not apply, any reduction on spending on the benefit by Westminster would have a knock-on effect on the Scottish government's budget.

How did universal credit change?

The government also wanted to reform universal credit (UC), external, and these changes went ahead after MPs backed the renamed Universal Credit Bill in Parliament and covers the whole of the UK.

The basic level of universal credit is £424.90 a month for a single person aged 25 or over.

Before the changes went through, if someone had limited capacity to work due to a disability or long-term condition, the payment more than doubled because of an incapacity top-up.

However, from April 2026, the health element of universal credit paid to new claimants was halved for those with less severe conditions.

The change did not affect the 2.8 million existing claimants of the health element.

Why does the government want to cut welfare spending?

In 2019, almost three million working-age adults (aged 16 to 64) in England and Wales claimed either disability or incapacity benefit. That is 1 in 13 of the population.

By March 2025, that had grown to about four million or 1 in 10, according to the IFS.

The rise has been fuelled by an increase in the number of claimants citing mental health conditions.

Welfare spending is forecast to rise by over a quarter between 2025 and 2030, with the main increases being sickness-related payouts for working age adults and pensioner benefits.

By cutting the amount it is paying out on welfare benefits, the more the government has to spend elsewhere.

articles.title: India pledges $1.6bn to Nepal in reset of ties
articles.description: As Nepal rebuilds after deadly floods, its prime minister sets contentious issues aside to secure Indian funding, port access and a new train service.
articles.content:
India pledges $1.6bn to Nepal in reset of ties

ByAzadeh Moshiri
South Asia Correspondent, Reporting fromDelhi
  • Published
    9 hours ago

Nepal's Prime Minister Balen Shah has repeatedly called for his country to be treated as an equal by its powerful neighbours. His first visit to the Indian capital, Delhi, put that approach to the test, as both sides sought to reset a relationship strained by years of friction.

The contrast between the two leaders was striking.

Shah, 36, wearing his trademark black suit and sunglasses, stood beside Prime Minister Narendra Modi, 76, dressed in white. Shah rose to power after a wave of Gen Z-led protests toppled his predecessor.

Modi, meanwhile, is serving a third term and has recently faced student-led protests in India.

Yet, the two leaders seemed determined to project warmer relations. They exchanged gifts, inspected a military guard of honour and jointly flagged off a new cross-border train service.

For Nepal, the stakes were about far more than repairing diplomatic ties.

The two countries announced a series of agreements covering trade, hydropower, transport and education for Nepali youths.

India, more crucially, unveiled a $1.6bn (£1.22bn) support package as Nepal recovers from devastating floods earlier this year.

The floods killed more than 1,400 people, with thousands still missing. Shah's government has faced criticism over support for families which lost homes and loved ones.

The country faces a huge reconstruction challenge. The government estimates rebuilding could cost as much as $4.8bn. Addressing the UN General Assembly in September, Shah warned that when climate disasters devastate poorer countries, "the answer cannot simply be another mega-loan".

Modi pledged nearly $1.6bn in Indian support. Most of it will come as a line of credit for energy projects, alongside about $400m in grants for reconstruction and infrastructure.

While Nepal would have preferred a larger package, former senior Nepali diplomat Vijay Kant Karna says it is still "a significant amount" and could help stabilise a relationship that has often been uneasy.

A Hindu-majority nation wedged between India and China, Nepal has long had to navigate competing interests from its two giant neighbours. Allegations of political interference and an unresolved border dispute have frequently complicated ties with India.

Nepal's former Prime Minister, KP Sharma Oli, who leads a communist party, was widely viewed as being closer to China. Shah, by contrast, emerged as a political outsider when he was elected earlier this year. The former rapper, then 35, led a party that was only four years old.

His new approach of dealing with India may explain why the border dispute was largely absent from the leaders' public remarks, although the joint statement acknowledged that outstanding issues remained.

According to Govind Pokharel, a former vice-chairman of Nepal's National Planning Commission, Shah's government may have chosen to set contentious issues aside in order to secure progress on more immediate development needs.

"Right now you can go home and convince the young Nepalis that it will be handled later," Pokhrel says, "but if they don't deal with these issues in the future, there will be criticism."

Veteran Indian diplomat Anil Trigunayat says both sides appear to have opted to leave the dispute to established mechanisms rather than engage in what he calls "cartographic aggressions".

There were other gains for Nepal as a result of the Delhi visit.

As a landlocked country heavily dependent on India for trade, Nepal secured access to two additional Indian ports, Kandla and Paradip. The two sides also agreed to improve road and rail connectivity.

The leaders jointly inaugurated a train service linking Ayodhya in India, revered by Hindus as the birthplace of Lord Ram, with Janakpur in Nepal, traditionally regarded as the birthplace of his wife Sita.

There was, however, disappointment on aviation.

Nepal has long sought greater access to Indian airspace in order to attract international traffic to its airports at Bhairahawa and Pokhara.

Some analysts believe the lack of an agreement reflects Indian concerns over Chinese involvement in the two airport projects.

"The airport in Pokhara can pose certain security challenges for India, so it is a more complicated issue to resolve," says Trigunayat.

India did, however, agree to make an existing air route linking Kathmandu, Bhairahawa and Lucknow bidirectional.

"Nepal invested a huge amount of money in those airports," says Pokharel. "It fell short of expectations, but the bidirectional route is a breakthrough."

Shah must now manage relations with China as he seeks to balance the interests of Nepal's two much larger neighbours.

For now he returns home with substantial financial commitments from India as Nepal continues the long task of rebuilding.

articles.title: Flights cancelled in Belgium due to cost-of-living strike
articles.description: A series of strikes have hit Belgium in recent months as the prime minister struggles to agree a budget to cut costs.
articles.content:
Flights cancelled in Belgium due to cost-of-living strike

ByPaulin Kola
  • Published
    23 November 2026, 11:26 GMT
Updated 9 hours ago

Hundreds of flights have been cancelled and public transport severely disrupted across Belgium as a result of a strike against planned austerity measures.

All air traffic has been halted at Brussels Airport in Zaventem as well as at Charleroi, home to low-cost airlines such as Ryanair.

Underground services have also been halted in capital Brussels, where large numbers of people joined a protest march.

The protest comes as Prime Minister Bart De Wever continues talks with his coalition allies over a budget to cut borrowing costs. King Philippe declined his resignation earlier this month, giving De Wever more time to negotiate.

No flights are taking off or landing at Brussels Airport between 07:00 and 21:00 local time (06:00-20:00 GMT) as a result of the strike by air traffic controllers.

"In total, 404 flights today cannot be operated, which has an impact on more than 50,000 passengers," Brussels Airport spokesperson Jeffrey Franssens said.

Reuters news agency spoke to Florence Faure, a French passenger who had arrived in Brussels from China's capital, Beijing, only to find that her flight to Paris Charles de Gaulle airport had been cancelled.

"Since our luggage was supposed to go on to Paris Charles de Gaulle, we didn't even collect it," she said.

A similar situation has affected Charleroi, where all flights were shown as "scheduled", regardless of the time of departure or arrival.

One passenger told Belgian broadcaster RTBF that she had received no warning and only discovered there were no flights when she arrived at the airport.

Philippe Naime, a teacher, was one of the tens of thousands taking part in the protest march in Brussels.

"Quite simply, no more money is being invested in education, and people are left to fend for themselves. But people do not have the means to do that," he told Reuters.

Public transport, schools and other public services are also facing disruptions.

The Belgian prime minister leads a five-party coalition.

One of its members, the socialist Vooruit, has been refusing to endorse plans agreed by the other four. It wants to raise taxes on the rich and for there to be fewer cuts to pensions and the health sector.

De Wever met King Philippe on Monday for the third update since the impasse.

"While expressing regret over the lack of significant progress, the king encouraged the prime minister to persevere in order to reach an agreement as soon as possible," the royal palace said in a statement.

The leader of one of the country's main unions, FGTB, said the government had alternatives to "dismantling the social protection system".

Bert Engelaar, head of the union, called for "a genuine wealth tax, fair taxation, and the elimination of tax loopholes".

"Political responsibility is not about keeping a government afloat at all costs. It's about knowing when to stop," he added, praising the Vooruit party.

Another union leader, Ann Vermorgen of the CSC, criticised government plans to cut bank holidays when they fall on weekends.

articles.title: Dylan Moran goes looking for trouble and disappears off the beaten track in this baffling comedy show
articles.description: Royal & Derngate, NorthamptonThe Black Books star gets off to a promising start as he contemplates ‘the burning ball of what you don’t understand’ but his search for levity leads to half-baked dittiesIs Dylan Moran joking when he opens his show by telling Northampton’s audience “I didn’t write anyth
articles.content:
Royal & Derngate, Northampton
The Black Books star gets off to a promising start as he contemplates ‘the burning ball of what you don’t understand’ but his search for levity leads to half-baked ditties

Is Dylan Moran joking when he opens his show by telling Northampton’s audience “I didn’t write anything, or prepare”? By the end, you wouldn’t bet on it. Bleary directionlessness may be par for the course for the Irish comic, whose work has always combined poetic-philosophical dazzle with a certain wooziness. But after a promising start tonight, his new touring show, Looking for Trouble, conspicuously loses its way, as Moran frets about forgetting a significant chunk of material, before abandoning his encore and leaving a bewildered audience in his wake.

That’s a shame, because there are shards of trademark brilliance in the opening 20 minutes, which see the 55-year-old address himself, albeit obliquely, to the mysteries of being human in 2026, AKA “the burning ball of what you don’t understand” From Trump to AI, Moran surveys it all in wide angle not closeup, as symptoms of our confusion, atavism and fear of expulsion from the tribe. The quality of his thinking in this section, while cheerfully offering himself up as Exhibit A in this prosecution of humanity’s perplexity, is arresting. And there are zingers, too, including a word-picture of the genitals that, once heard, may never be forgotten.

articles.title: How a billionaire tax proposal failed in California despite big election wins for progressives
articles.description: In an election with major wins for Democrats and progressives nationwide, California voters not only rejected the biggest test yet for a state wealth tax, they also approved a measure making it much harder to enact one in the future.
articles.content:
By —

Sophie Austin, Associated Press Sophie Austin, Associated Press

  • https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/how-a-billionaire-tax-proposal-failed-in-california-despite-big-election-wins-for-progressives
  • Email

How a billionaire tax proposal failed in California despite big election wins for progressives

Politics Nov 23, 2026 8:27 AM EST

SACRAMENTO, Calif. (AP) — In an election with major wins for Democrats and progressives nationwide, California voters not only rejected the biggest test yet for a state wealth tax, they also approved a measure making it much harder to enact one in the future.

Proposition 40 would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, with most of the money dedicated to healthcare. Just more than half — 52% — of voters rejected it. Meanwhile, they narrowly approved Proposition 42, which bans the state from enacting future taxes on people's financial assets. State lawmakers can't override that; it can only be undone by voters with a future ballot measure.

READ MORE: California voters reject tax on net worth of billionaires

"I don't think you're going to see such a good Democratic electorate in the near future," said Wesley Hussey, a political science professor at California State University, Sacramento. "This was the time to pass something that was pretty lefty and progressive and had a lot of opposition."

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

Nationally it was a good year for so-called "tax the rich" measures in other states, including Washington, where voters upheld a 9.9% tax on household income over $1 million. But California's measure was different because it would have taxed the assets, not the income, of the ultrarich.

And it targeted billionaires, who are significantly wealthier than millionaires and have far more assets to spend. A committee that opposed Proposition 40 and backed Proposition 42 raised more than $333 million, including large donations from tech billionaires such as Google co-founder Sergey Brin and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt. Collectively, the fight over taxing billionaires was one of the most expensive ballot battles in state history.

READ MORE: Voters decide key ballot measures on abortion rights, congressional redistricting and voter ID laws

Outside observers say the fact that it failed in California, a heavily Democratic state often viewed as a liberal leader, is not surprising because of the sheer amount of money spent opposing it and the big-name Democrats who lined up against it. Gov. Gavin Newsom was among those warning it was a bad financial deal for the state. Opponents outspent supporters by 10 to 1.

But proponents of the wealth tax, which included SEIU United Healthcare Workers West, U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders and U.S. Rep. Ro Khanna, are trying to frame the loss as progress toward holding billionaires accountable in the future. They have teased bringing the idea before voters again in 2028.

"The game is up, people have had it and this election is just the beginning," Khanna said on election night.

The proposal was controversial from the beginning

Faced with pushback from Newsom, SEIU UHW offered to scale back its proposal in June just before it qualified for the ballot. The union proposed a 2% levy, down from 5%, but Newsom's office said the proposed tax remained fundamentally flawed. Efforts to make a deal fell apart, and the union proceeded despite a growing coalition of groups opposing the tax.

Opponents of the tax said its failure affirmed that voters understood the risks associated with it. They warned it would have driven billionaires and their tax money out of state, causing budget problems down the road. California relies heavily on the rich for its income tax revenue.

READ MORE: A guide to the key ballot measures voters will decide on Election Day

"We were hopefully optimistic based on the polls that voters would agree with us that Prop. 40 was just a horrible idea for the state and Prop. 42 provides some important protections going forward," said David Kline, a spokesperson for the California Taxpayers Association.

California voters didn't completely repudiate the concept of taxing the wealthy at higher rates in this year's election. They approved a measure to indefinitely extend a tax increase on individual incomes exceeding $371,000 to raise money for education.

Higher taxes on millionaires passed in other states

Besides Washington, Colorado voters adopted a graduated income tax that imposes higher rates on people with higher income, including an 8.4% tax on income over $1 million. The revenue from both states' taxes will go toward education, healthcare and other services. Spending on the Washington and Colorado measures paled in comparison to the billionaire tax battle. Legislatures in Hawaii, Maine and Rhode Island also approved new taxes this year on people with incomes over $1 million.

California has a 1% income tax on millionaires that voters approved in 2004 to raise money for mental health services.

Carl Davis, research director at the nonprofit Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy, said the results indicated "a really good batting average" for backers of higher taxes for the wealthy. California's billionaire tax effort was hurt by divisions among organized labor over the measure, he said.

"I think the pendulum is swinging toward increased interest in taxing the rich," he said.

Advocates for higher taxes on the wealthy plan to expand their push next year in a half-dozen states where Democrats recently won control of both legislative chambers and the governor's office, said Amber Wallin, executive director of the State Revenue Alliance, a nonprofit advocacy group for progressive tax policies.

"I think that the movement will only continue to grow," Wallin said.

California could revisit higher taxes on the ultrawealthy

California's Proposition 42 bans new taxes on people's financial assets, business interests and intellectual property, as well as taxes that apply retroactively. The billionaire tax, for instance, would have applied to people living in the state as of Jan. 1, 2026, even though it would have taken effect the following year. That will now be prohibited.

California Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra, a Democrat who will take over from Newsom in January, opposed the billionaire tax. But he said recently that the amount of support it received sent "a clear signal" that people "don't believe everybody in California is paying their fair share." He said he wanted to correct that but didn't specify how.

Lorena Gonzalez, president of the California Federation of Labor Unions, which supported Proposition 40, said opposition from groups like the California Teachers Association and Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California made it harder to pass the measure than if supporters had been fighting billionaires alone.

But she said this year's ballot fight was just the start.

"We have to go back to the ballot," Gonzalez said. "We've got to keep fighting."

Associated Press writer David A. Lieb in Jefferson City, Missouri, contributed.
